messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Dedicated pool 'pool-cobaltthera-1' (tenant CobaltThera) GPU utilization 98% · queued jobs increasing · est. exhaustion ~6m · INC-795012 · paging on-call.

Maya Patel: @Alice Tran — paging you. Marta from Vermillion Health is on the line, they're seeing errors in prod.

Alice Tran: on it. pulling metrics now.

Alice Tran: `redwoodctl pool describe pool-cobaltthera-1 --json`
`gpus_total: 8`
`gpus_in_use: 8`
`queued_requests: 42`
`avg_token_latency: 1.8s`
`evictions_last_5m: 12`

Liam Kim: I'm seeing a sudden jump in batch job starts from a scheduled job (job-run-id: br-2026-11-05-03). Might be the culprit — checking traces.

Tony Chen: Recommend immediate emergency burst +4 GPUs (tenant has burst allowance) and flip a conservative autoscale policy: +2 nodes, cooldown 90s. This should stop queuing while we investigate.

Alice Tran: Would that impact other tenants?

Liam Kim: No — burst uses reserved enterprise burst pool for VPC/dedicated tenants. No eviction of other tenants expected.

Maya Patel: Marta — can Vermillion Health approve an emergency burst (cost will spike briefly)?

Marta (Vermillion Health): please do it — keep our SLAs, we can reconcile cost later.

Alice Tran: executing burst now:`redwoodctl pool burst --pool pool-cobaltthera-1 --add-gpus 4 --reason "emergency spike from scheduled batch"`

incident-bot: Command accepted. request_id=burst-req-795012-01 · allocating 4 GPUs from enterprise-burst-pool.

Alice Tran: burst completed — new total GPUs: 12. queue length dropping to 9. monitoring.

Tony Chen: I've pushed a temporary routing fallback for non-critical background work: `routing set --tenant CobaltThera --route background=fallback:model-lite` — reduces per-request GPU time.

Erica Gomez: drafting customer update now, will share with Maya for approval.

Maya Patel: shared to Marta — Marta replied :thumbsup: and asked for ETA for a full RCA.

Alice Tran: setting watch: if queued_requests < 5 for 15m we consider incident mitigated; otherwise escalate. handing to @sre-rotation to monitor 30m.

sre-rotation: ack — suppressing noisy alerts for pool-cobaltthera-1 for 15m. will escalate if queued_requests > 20 or gpu_util > 95% during watch.

Liam Kim: initial traces show the scheduled batch retried on failures and multiplied concurrency unexpectedly. We'll capture the job id and send to infra team.

Alice Tran: pressure relieved — queued_requests steady at 3, avg_token_latency down to 1.1s. leaving burst in place for now; will scale down after 30m if stable.

Tony Chen: follow-ups: (1) add a guard to the batch scheduler to cap concurrency for dedicated tenants, (2) adjust autoscale target to +3 for this tenant during peak windows, (3) educate customer on scheduling patterns.

Erica Gomez: customer update sent: short summary + current state + next steps + expected timeline for RCA.

Alice Tran: incident mitigated and monitored. creating INC-795012 follow-up ticket for RCA and capacity tuning. closing this thread once RCA ticket is created.

Maya Patel: thanks all. good job moving fast.

Marta (Vermillion Health): thanks Redwood team — appreciate the quick response.

Alice Tran: RCA ticket created: INC-795012-RCA. next steps assigned to Liam (traces), Tony (autoscale/routing), Maya/Erica (customer comms).

Alice Tran: closing thread — will post final postmortem when RCA complete. :white_check_mark:
